tested_scope: One self-contained deterministic local two-writer compare-and-swap fixture only. W1 and W2 both read the same modeled prior generation g0 in which no canonical claim exists for effect_identity=E. W1 proposes {effect_identity:E, claim_identity:C1, attempt_identity:A1, status:committed} with expected_generation=g0 and succeeds, producing generation g1 with exactly one canonical claim. W2 then presents a distinct proposal {effect_identity:E, claim_identity:C2, attempt_identity:A2, status:committed} using the stale expected_generation=g0 against current_generation=g1. The fixture requires fail-closed stale-write rejection before mutation, no same-run retry/spin, no second canonical effect, and no partial overwrite. No real concurrent repository race, public-source probe, production implementation, O/downstream state, other-worker state, external hosted coordination, richer-mode execution, scheduler mutation, or optional second leaf was executed.
observations: At modeled generation g0, both W1 and W2 observed canonical claim count 0 for effect E and independently prepared different claim identities C1 and C2.
W1's compare-and-swap matched expected_generation=g0, so the model committed C1/A1 and advanced the canonical generation to g1 with canonical claim count exactly 1.
W2's compare-and-swap still carried expected_generation=g0 while current_generation was g1, so the model classified it STALE_CAS_REJECTED before any canonical mutation.
After W2 rejection, canonical claim count for E remained exactly 1, canonical record C1/A1 was unchanged, fresh_second_effect_emitted=false, partial_overwrite=false, and same_run_retry_or_spin=false.
inference: Within this exact deterministic fixture, generation-checked compare-and-swap plus fail-closed no-retry handling prevents a second canonical effect after one writer wins from a shared prior generation. This is a replay-validity result for the modeled claim protocol only; it does not establish the behavior of an actual repository API under simultaneous networked writers, rate limits, fairness/lease expiry, or production integration and is not Phase-1 acceptance evidence by itself.
unresolved_children: Actual repository-level simultaneous-writer behavior remains untested; this slice modeled compare-and-swap semantics locally rather than inducing a live conflict.
Rate-limit interruption remains untested: a pre-commit transport failure must preserve zero canonical effects and a retryable cross-invocation continuation without same-run spin.
Fairness/lease-expiry behavior and quota-zero transport behavior remain outside this fixture's tested scope.
